name: Nederlof-Wegrzycki OV reduction for Subset Sum and Belova-Chukhin-Kulikov-Mihajlin space improvement
description: Nederlof and Wegrzycki (STOC 2021) combine Schroeppel-Shamir with the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique to reduce worst-case Subset Sum to many instances of Orthogonal Vectors on {0,1}^d vectors with support d/4, giving the first improvement over Schroeppel-Shamir: time O*(2^{0.5n}) with space O*(2^{0.249999n}) (instead of 2^{n/4}). Belova, Chukhin, Kulikov and Mihajlin (ESA 2024) simplify the algorithm and analysis and reduce the space to O*(2^{0.246n}) by also filtering lists with a random prime inside Schroeppel-Shamir, yielding more but smaller weighted OV instances. The OV step is the matching/disjointness step that rules out pseudosolutions (elements used twice) produced by representations, which is the same disjointness test needed to pick out disjoint equal-sum pairs.
authors_year_venue: J. Nederlof, K. Wegrzycki, Improving Schroeppel and Shamir's algorithm for subset sum via orthogonal vectors, STOC 2021 (arXiv 2010.08576); T. Belova, N. Chukhin, A. S. Kulikov, I. Mihajlin, Improved Space Bounds for Subset Sum, ESA 2024 (arXiv 2402.13170)
status_and_verification: Peer-reviewed (STOC 2021, ESA 2024). Abstracts (via search/fetch) checked; the CJRS paper's description of the OV subroutine (Section 1.2) was also read. Full proofs of NW21 and BCKM24 were NOT read. [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: NW21: randomized O*(2^{0.5n}) time and O*(2^{0.249999n}) space for worst-case Subset Sum with n integers; OV algorithm detecting an orthogonal pair among N vectors in {0,1}^d with support size d/4 in time O~(N * 2^{d}/d^{d/4}) (as stated in abstract via search snippet, formula typeset not verified). BCKM24: O*(2^{0.5n}) time, O*(2^{0.246n}) space. [uncertain]
regime_exponents: Time is exactly the n/2 baseline (no time saving); only space moves from 0.25n to 0.249999n to 0.246n. No relation to D* <= 2^{0.311n} or 0.661n thresholds.
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial and probabilistic: Schroeppel-Shamir 4-list split, representation technique with random-prime filtering (Howgrave-Graham-Joux), reduction to (weighted) Orthogonal Vectors with a dedicated OV algorithm for low-weight vectors.
quantitative_loss: Only sub-exponential/poly losses in time; the space saving is a small exponential constant (0.0010...0.004n). No structural theorem, so no BSG/PFR style loss is involved.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case for Subset Sum (randomization is internal via random primes); no average-case assumption.
coefficient_set: {0,1} subset sums (Subset Sum); representation step temporarily uses extended coefficients ({0,1,2}-type) and OV removes pseudosolutions.
subset_size_regime: All subsets; the OV vectors have a fixed relative support (d/4) from the Schroeppel-Shamir split, not a Theta(n)-subset constraint on solutions.
relevance_to_Nc: The OV/disjointness step is exactly what finds a disjoint equal-sum pair among colliding candidates; N_c measures how many such candidate pairs exist. If N_c is large the matching stage has many valid outputs, which may allow subsampled/filtered runs with a smaller list (an unproved route).
relevance_to_Dstar: None directly. A small D* (few distinct balanced half-sums) would mean OV lists have many repeated sums, making hash-bucketing cheaper, but the papers do not exploit this.
applicability_gap: No time improvement over 2^{n/2}; structure (density, doubling) is not used. Handles space only. Pseudosolution removal assumes lists built from the representation technique, not general bins of colliding Theta(n)-subsets.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: None specific; hard instances are generic (random 2^{Omega(n)} bit integers) where the algorithm runs at 2^{n/2}.
dependency_chain: Schroeppel-Shamir -> representation technique (HGJ) -> OV (NW21) -> prime filtering (BCKM24); CJRS poly-saving reuses the OV + representation combination; a structural dichotomy (C1/C2) would supply the 'few distinct sums' branch.
lean_formalizable: Algorithmic probability analysis; low priority. Only the combinatorial counting of representations might be formalizable.
computational_check: Source reports no large-scale experiments (theoretical). Not checkable by repo scripts at n<=40 in a meaningful way (asymptotic gains). [uncertain]
next_experiment: Implement the representation + OV filter at n<=30 and measure how many pseudosolutions vs true disjoint pairs survive, to calibrate how N_c interacts with the matching step.
open_issues: A time bound below 2^{n/2} remains open (the central open problem); only poly saving known (CJRS). Whether the 0.246n space can be pushed to 0.25n/2 or to poly space with 2^{n/2} time is open. Details of the constant 0.249999 vs exact value not verified. [uncertain]
